title: Resolve mini-deadlock in continuous batcher during Dedicated cross-region failover causing short-request suppression
creator: Jordan Patel
description:
Summary: A high-severity customer escalation reported sustained short-request latency spikes and apparent request suppression during a Dedicated cross-region failover. Investigation shows a short-lived mini-deadlock in the continuous batcher admission/dispatch path when tenant failover signals coincide with inflight region drain and autoscaler shifts. Consequence: small/latency-sensitive requests were delayed for multiple seconds while large long-context inflight windows held KV handoffs and admission leases, causing customer-visible long-context tail and quota backpressure.

Observed behavior and impact: Multiple customers on Dedicated pools (cross-region failover enabled) saw 95th/99th token latency regressions and elevated error rates for low-context calls during the failover window. Logs show admission leases not expiring cleanly while inflight-window accounting deferred preemptive dequeues. The platform's automatic fallback to alternate model variants was suppressed because the admission controller believed the host still owned KV ranges. This caused request accumulation and short-request starvation for ~30-90s during the worst incidents.

Root cause hypothesis: When a region failover event and autoscaler-driven host reassignments occur concurrently, the admission window state machine can enter a transient state where inflight reservations are neither released nor force-transferred. The continuous batcher scheduler uses a tick-driven admission expiry that assumes stable host membership; cross-region churn exposes a race that prevents short-request preemption and forces long-context windows to persist beyond their expected lifetime.

Temporary mitigations applied: - Instituted an emergency ingress slow-down for affected Dedicated pools to limit new long-context admissions. - Enabled a control-plane coordinated drain signal for the failing region to accelerate KV handoff. - Rolled out a manual canary with feature-flagged early-dequeue to the most impacted customers to restore short-request throughput.

Proposed long-term fix: 1) Add region-failover-aware admission expiry: on failover detection, immediately shorten admission lease TTLs and trigger force-dequeue passes for length-heterogeneous queues. 2) Introduce a "dedicated-drain-handshake" to explicitly transfer KV ownership and unblock inflight windows across regions. 3) Implement a conservative preemptive shortflow reservation token (length-aware inflight reservation) to guarantee a minimum throughput for short requests during churn. 4) Add telemetry and GA alerts: new SLO metrics for "forced-dequeue frequency", "admission-lease-aging", and a dashboard correlating autoscaler events, failover signals, and continuous-batcher stalls.

Risk/trade-offs: Force-dequeue can increase reorder or quality variability for multi-token long-context responses; we will gate via feature flag and tune thresholds. Accelerating lease expiry during failover may cause extra KV handoffs and transient replays for some in-flight long requests; but the trade-off favors short-request availability for latency-sensitive applications.

Testing and rollout plan: - Unit & integration tests added to the scheduler harness to simulate concurrent failover + autoscaler churn. - Add fault-injection litmus tests in staging (chaos): host removal, region routing switch, and long-context flood. - Canary rollout behind feature flag in runtime-1.22: 5% Dedicated clusters -> 20% -> 100% with 24h observation windows between steps. - Private customers: deliver patch as optioned upgrade with clear release notes and a checklist for upgrade windows.

Telemetry & postmortem: Capture detailed traces for the incident and include in postmortem doc. Postmortem draft created; follow-ups include backport for earlier runtime patchlines and a documentation update for Dedicated failover runbooks.
comments: 2026-03-01: Triage call with SE and oncall. Customer reported reproducible spikes during scheduled cross-region switch. Assigned to Ava Martinez.

2026-03-02: Reproduced in lab by simulating region drain + long-context steady load. Observed admission leases not expiring for ~45s. Linked traces: https://monitoring.redwood.ai/d/abcd123/batcher-failover?orgId=1

2026-03-03: Hotpatch deployed to affected Dedicated pools that shortens admission TTLs to 2s during detected failover windows. Immediate improvement for one customer. Hotpatch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345

2026-03-05: Engineering review: trade-off discussion. Agreed to implement coordinated drain-handshake + preemptive shortflow reservation instead of aggressive global TTL shrinkage. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELIABILITY/Dedicated+Failover+Batcher+Incident
2026-03-08: Integration tests added to scheduler harness and chaos job created. Test results: preemptive reservation prevents >90% of short-request suppression cases in simulated failover.
2026-03-10: PR opened for feature-flagged implementation of force-dequeue + drain-handshake: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12401. Requesting review from Kai Chen and Morgan Lee.
2026-03-12: Customer comms drafted and reviewed by Support & Product. Plan to include upgrade notes and rollback instructions. Preparing canary rollout starting 2026-03-14.
